heard: Undocking to escape a spinning spacecraft made Gemini 8 spin even faster. Command pilot Neil Armstrong and pilot David Scott launched aboard Gemini 8 on March 16, 1966. The mission successfully achieved the world's first orbital docking with an Agena target vehicle. Minutes later, a short-circuited thruster threw the joint spacecraft into an uncontrollable role. Believing the target vehicle was malfunctioning, the crew undocked while out of radio range. Without the Agena's mass, the capsule accelerated to nearly one revolution per second. Armstrong fired the reentry thrusters to halt the tumble, consuming 75% of their maneuvering fuel. Safety rules forced an emergency splashdown in the western Pacific Ocean.
